title: Set an exam table's stirrups: draw each out, unfold it, lift it out of its lock and drop it into the outermost notch
instruction: Set this exam table's stirrups for an exam: both out, unfolded and locked in their outermost positions.
context: Setting the stirrups is part of preparing the room for a pelvic examination: about 44.2 million were performed in the US in 2012 (USPSTF evidence review, JAMA 2017, from CDC survey data; about 34.7 million in 2018), typically in the lithotomy position with the feet in the table's stirrups. Each stirrup is drawn out, unfolded, lifted out of its lateral lock and let down into a notch; the maker's guide warns "Be sure the stirrups are locked in place before using". The wrong state that looks right: a stirrup swung out and let go between positions rests unlocked on the lock's teeth. The parts hold the order: a folded stirrup cannot turn up inside the shelf, and a bar swings only with its end lifted. Unlike a suitcase handle drawn out to its lock (TK-28LP2A), each stirrup chains five gated motions, one arm per side.
setup: Two YAM arms (pads open 94 mm), bases 61 cm apart at the near edge of the bench. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x out, y left; heights above the bench. The foot end of an exam table's stirrup shelf, built as the bench fixture in fabrication/ (drawings, printable parts and bill of materials; built to the motions of a Midmark Ritter 204's stirrups: draw, unfold, lift and drop into a notch): a 67 x 58 x 22 cm box clamped to the bench, its front face at x 65, centred on y 0, its rear 32 cm overhanging onto a stand; two 9 x 4.2 cm windows in the face. Two stirrup assemblies, bars at y +-24.5, 14 cm up: each a 3/4 x 1/4 in steel bar 56.5 cm long (0.60 kg with the T-rail under it), held from below by a pivot boss 5 cm behind the face; a 0.30 kg stirrup (25 cm from its roll pin to the tip of a 7 cm wide teardrop loop) on the roll pin at the bar's front end, folded flat along the bar; a 6 mm detent post 3 cm tall on the bar's tail, pressed up (about 11 N) into an 8 mm wide, 5 mm deep groove along the draw and notches at 12 deg inward, straight, 12 and 24 deg outward. Start: both stowed, the roll pin 2 cm in front of the face; each bar draws 40 cm to its collar (the pin then 42 cm out). Both arms at their ready poses, grippers open.
scoring: Checked with a rule, a protractor on the boss and the trial video once everything is still. Per stirrup: 2 points if set, 1 if out, 0 otherwise. Out: drawn to within 8 mm of its collar (the roll pin at least 41.2 of the 42 cm out from the face) and unfolded (within 5 deg of its open stop). Set: out and locked in the outermost notch: the bar within 2 deg of 24 deg outward and within 1.5 deg of level, the post up in that notch. A stirrup earns its points only once both grippers have been at least 3 cm from it and it has been still, both for the last 1 s (in simulation no point of it moves more than 1 mm; in a real trial no visible motion in the last second of the video); a stirrup still held or moving earns 0, and the other still counts. Score: points / 4 (0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0). 0 for good if a stirrup is ever forced 3 deg or 3 mm past one of its stops.
reset_notes: For each stirrup: lift its end slightly, swing it straight until the post drops into the groove's end, fold the stirrup flat along its bar, and push the bar into the shelf until only the stirrup's hinge end (38 mm) shows. Arms to their ready poses.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at the fixture's dimensions, which are the model's by construction (the Midmark table's are not published); shelf fixed. Free joints with real stops and light damping: the boss's swing, the bar's lift and draw, the stirrup's roll pin. The order is held by contact: the window over the folded stirrup, the lock's groove and notches on the post. The fixture's lock spring, 2.13 N/mm at the post, is modelled as 12 N m/rad at the lift joint.
